paragraphs.text: He was not of that king of Scotland’s mind, who seldom asked counsel, and never followed any. But though himself were full of wisdom, yet he advised with his subjects about the weighty work he had in hand. See Pro 11:22; Pro 20:18; Pro 24:6. His first care was to establish religion; as the first thing Abraham did in any place he moved to, was to set up an altar. "Seek first the kingdom of God," &c.
Thus he both getteth their good wills and underfeeleth how they stood affected to God’s sincere service.
paragraphs.anchor: If it seem good unto you.

paragraphs.text: If he hinder it not by any oracle, or cross accident; but assist and succeed our enterprise.
paragraphs.anchor: And that it be of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Erumpamus, dimittamus. Let us break forth and send; that is, let us send speedily and effectually. See his zeal for the Lord of hosts.
So he calleth all his subjects. The great Turk counteth and calleth them all his slaves.
He was so vexed with his enemies without and a spirit of envy and ambition within, that he minded not the ark. Mark here how David faults himself among others as negligent. So Ezr 9:7-15 Dan 9:5-15.
paragraphs.anchor: For we inquired not at it in the days of Saul.

paragraphs.text: Jovianus the Emperor was wont to wish that he might govern wise men, and that wise men might govern him. David had this happiness.
paragraphs.anchor: And all the congregation said that they would do so.

paragraphs.text: Called elsewhere the torrent of Egypt, {Num 34:5} which some take for a river running near to Rhinocolura; but others for Nile, that ancient river whose seven streams of old are now become four, as travellers tell us. The name Sichor hath a notion of blackness in it, from the blackness of the water, or rather of the mud and slime that it brings down with it; or the black colour of the grounds and soils it passeth through. {a}
{a} The Ethiopians called it Sius; the Greeks, Mελας; the Latins, Melo. - Richard.
Called also Kirjathbaal. {Jos 15:60} For more notes on this and the following verses, see on 2Sa 6:2-10. {See Trapp on "2Sa 6:2"} &c
This was ill done by such a holy convention. Councils may err.
How should we rejoice in the gospel now restored! O nos ingratos!
Psallunt et saliunt. All this is no warrant for those Popish pompous processions and superstitous will-worships.
God must be duly worshipped, lest instead of a blessing we meet with a blow; lest instead of making up the breach we become makers of breaches, as here.
At himself, I think; at his own and the people’s error in carting the ark: else he was much mistaken. See on 2Sa 6:8.

To perpetuate the memory of that signal judgment. So Num 9:3; Num 22:3 Jos 7:26. For this end also, the brazen censors of those presumptuous sinners against their own souls, were nailed as broad plates upon the altar, {Num 16:39-40} for a warning to others.
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore that place was called Perezuzza.

paragraphs.anchor: And David was afraid of God.

paragraphs.text: Why, well enough, if you will take but better heed to the manner; which is either the making or marring of any action. But David was frightened, and for present, unresolved. So suddenly can God change the scene; dash all our comforts, -
